description: Continuity of a principal across a key change, signed by the predecessor (first signer) and the successor (second signer). At most one outgoing edge per predecessor and one incoming per successor; no self-edge; no cycle. Authority bound to the predecessor follows the successor by sequence; the predecessor's later signatures remain valid, printed as post-succession.

claims: both keys signed this record at the recorded position: the predecessor named the successor and the successor proved possession by signing
no earlier unrevoked Succession names this predecessor or this successor
doesNotClaim: which holder of a shared or stolen predecessor key acted — a revoked and re-made succession is printed as contested, and endorsers decide whom they endorse next
that the recorded actor is any particular person, organization, or agent beyond the key that signed — a name is a claim; a key id is the identity
